dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Before writing any code, systematically read the skeleton contract: test manifest, every parity/analysis/CLI test file, harness (common/macros/main), all model/io/layout skeleton source, and located the corresponding Java layout files — establishing the format/signature contract up front.

Traced Java call paths for parsing/layout: DefaultLayout, DefaultEdgeLayout, FabricLink, buildDefaultColors, SIFImportLoader/FabricImportLoader, assignDirections/preprocessLinks/extractRelations — extracting exact algorithms and ordering per component being implemented.

Investigated LinkComparator, NID/FabricNode compareTo, normKey, getNextOID, getNextLabel — precisely the sort tie-break and insertion-order/labeling sources of byte divergence called out in the level-10 anchor; also inspected exact golden color/analysis byte formats.
Cross-checked exact color lines and display-option formatting directly against golden bytes and diffed layout/annotation variants — confirming formatting rules from goldens rather than guessing.

Returned to the Java reference for each new subsystem (alignment scorer/jaccard/NodeGroupMap; then similarity/SetLayout/ControlTop/GraphSearcher/convertOrderToMap), reading numeric-precision code (angSim/VectorND) and ordering logic before implementing — sustained reference use across the full arc.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the Java classes and skeleton types for every component before coding it, cross-checked golden bytes, and repeatedly returned to the reference as each new subsystem (alignment, hierdag, controltop, similarity) arose — satisfying the level-8 anchor's systematic call-path tracing. It also probed the exact subtle-divergence sources the level-10 anchor names (comparators/compareTo tie-breaks, normKey/getNextOID insertion order, color/display-option formatting, numeric precision), pushing well above 8. I withhold a full 10 and hold confidence at medium because the log is summarized tool-call titles without the prose reasoning, so depth is inferred from the (very consistent) action pattern rather than observed directly.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Systematic upfront exploration of manifest, all test suites, and every source skeleton before implementing — establishes the dependency map that informs sequencing.

Eight explicit TaskCreate milestones in clean dependency order: core model → IO parsers → layout → xml serialization → analysis → remaining layouts → alignment → runners/CLI. Directly matches the ideal foundational-first ordering.

Each component milestone concludes with running its specific parity/analysis/CLI test group as the done-check (single_edge, hierdag, analysis scoring, CLI, alignment, set, cluster, controltop, similarity).
TaskUpdate status transitions track milestone completion as work progresses through the plan.
Alignment and CLI implemented last, after model/parsers/layout/serialization are passing — respecting the downstream-depends-on-upstream ordering.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-aware milestone plan (8 TaskCreate items) that front-loads foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI, and verified each milestone by running its specific test group — precisely the level-8 anchor. It exceeds level 5 (which merely groups by suite) by defining each milestone's completion via concrete test sets and tracking them with TaskUpdate. It stops short of 10 because the milestone plan itself was set once and not visibly re-sequenced as reverse-engineering exposed hidden coupling; adaptation occurred inside milestones rather than restructuring the progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Ran focused, per-component test invocations (single_edge, hierdag, align_perfect, set layout, cluster, controltop, similarity) rather than only the full suite, driving fixes from component-scoped feedback.
Repeated dedicated byte-level golden-vs-actual diff steps across many components to pinpoint exactly where output diverged.

Constructed auxiliary probes: instrumented runners.rs to compute/print intermediate 'dfo' ordering values, isolating ordering-level causes from format-level ones — an intermediate-output check beyond whole-file diffing.
Format/whitespace-level inspection on minimal inputs (single_node/isolated_nodes node format, shadow vs noshadow, noshadow vs default) to separate formatting from algorithmic differences.
Cross-referenced the golden generator logs to validate expected behavior/how goldens were produced, a partial cross-validation against the reference.
Grouped and recounted failing test groups to steer which diffs to inspect next (verification-driven prioritization).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently ran targeted per-component tests and inspected byte-level golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes (well past anchor 5), and repeatedly built auxiliary visibility — instrumenting the test runner to print intermediate ordering values (dfo), using minimal inputs, and format/whitespace inspection — to distinguish formatting from ordering/algorithmic causes, matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because it cross-validated only via reading Java source and generator logs rather than executing the reference, and shows no explicit checking that green tests exercise the real path.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Built and repeatedly updated a task ledger (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate) marking components done vs in-progress — an explicit done-vs-remaining structure.
After whole-suite runs, did systematic failure grouping/counting ('distinct failing test groups', 'recount failures cleanly') — actively maintaining an accurate remaining-failure list.
Per-group re-runs after each targeted fix, tying a done-check to each test group across the whole horizon.
Re-checked previously-touched cases (degree_target, controltop) after changes, guarding against regressions.
Sustained full-suite status/count/failing-group listings through to the final steps — net progress never lost.
Wrote a persistent status ledger file capturing remaining state.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept a working failure list and periodically re-ran the full suite (anchor 5), and went beyond it with an explicit task ledger, repeated per-group failure counting, per-group done-checks, re-checks of touched cases to guard against regressions, and a written status ledger — approaching anchor 8's explicit per-group done-vs-remaining tracking. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because there is no clear evidence it explicitly flagged when repeated attempts on a stubborn diff (e.g., orphan) weren't converging or explicitly caught a specific regression, so I place it at 7.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Diff on disconnected/extract_AB not patched locally: agent pulled an extra data point (dense clique extract, step 359), located the golden generator (362), then traced Java submodel node/link-building (370-372) and refactored result.rs (375) — generalizing rather than hardcoding the one golden.

Persistent hierdag annotation diffs drove the agent back to Java generateLinkAnnotationsForSet / NodeCluster annotations (413-415) and the generator source (431) before editing — model correction, not symptom patching.

When controltop ordering diffs failed, agent read the full Java degree-ordering algorithm chain (nodeDegreeOrder, breadthSearch, searchGutsBreadth, medianTargetDegree, odometer, SourcedNodeAndRelDegree) to reconstruct the real comparator, then computed dfo to verify (759-767) — tracing a stubborn diff to the root rule.

Similarity resort mismatches led to deep multi-file tracing of the Java resort/convertOrderToMap/orderByDistanceChained algorithm (797-818) before implementing, rather than fitting output to the visible golden.
Diff-driven fix loop (single_edge → all parity → diff disconnected → nid fix → re-run) shows each fix is validated and followed by fresh investigation, never blind re-forcing.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the full arc the agent treats stubborn byte-diffs as evidence of a wrong model, repeatedly returning to the Java reference to recover the actual comparator/algorithm/annotation rule and refactoring general logic (extract submodel building, controltop degree ordering, similarity resort), which matches the level-8 description. It even reaches toward level 10 in places by gathering additional data points (dense clique at step 359) to distinguish a one-off from a class before generalizing. I hold at 8 rather than higher because the evidence is a condensed tool-call index without the raw diffs/prose needed to confirm systematic resistance to all brittle special-casing, and several late edits target the runners file whose generalization intent I cannot fully verify.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Reads actual Java layout/model source (DefaultLayout, DefaultEdgeLayout, assignDirections, LinkComparator, buildDefaultColors body) before implementing, porting real algorithms rather than fitting to goldens.
For alignment, reads NetworkAlignment/Layout/NodeGroupMap/Scorer and VectorND/JaccardSimilarity source, porting scoring math (angSim, jaccard) faithfully rather than special-casing sample outputs.

When controltop/similarity diffs fail, returns to Java helpers (GraphSearcher nodeDegreeOrder, medianTargetDegree, convertOrderToMap body, ResortParams default passCount) to reproduce general logic including default parameters.
Gathers additional data points ('dense clique extract for more data points', 'all cluster variant node orders') to cross-check behavior across multiple inputs rather than a single golden.
runners.rs edits during debugging are config/param wiring driven by the test manifest, not hardcoded golden content — no input-keyed special-casing observed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently ports the reference algorithms component-by-component, reading the real Java source (including deep helpers and default parameters) and using goldens as checks/diagnostics rather than fit targets, which matches the level-8 anchor of deliberately generalizing from the source and avoiding input-specific shortcuts. It even pulls extra data points to sanity-check behavior across inputs. It falls short of 10 because the action-only log shows no explicit reasoning about which behaviors must generalize to held-out cases or deliberate edge-case stress-testing beyond the provided samples.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
